defect.finding_source: Adversarial QA Agent RT-2/RT-3, independently verified by orchestrator against the artifact
defect.symptom: d4_additives array omitted aspartame (E951) and acesulfame-K (E950) on 4 drinkable GO products, despite the ingredient string declaring 'ממתיקים (אספרטיים, אססולפאם k)' explicitly.
defect.root_cause: GLASSBOX_W2_ADDITIVES dictionary in constants.py matched aspartame/acesulfame-K only via their standard spellings ('אספרטם' / 'אצסולפם' with tzadi) or E-number. The 4 GO products (and 12 spoonable products, found by corpus-wide scan) declare the same additives via a bare-name variant spelling using samech instead of tzadi ('אספרטיים' / 'אססולפאם') and no E-number on-pack -- so detect_additives_d4()'s substring match against match_patterns_he never fired. Contrast: the 'Pro' drinks (7290110573737, 7290110552244) use the tzadi spelling ('אצסולפאם') already in the table, so they matched correctly -- confirming the gap is specifically the samech bare-name spelling, not a structural bug in detect_additives_d4() itself.

fix.change_summary: Added samech-spelling bare-name variants to match_patterns_he for two existing GLASSBOX_W2_ADDITIVES entries (no new entries, no tier/function_he/cosmetic_mup changes): E951 (aspartame) gained ['אספרטיים', 'אספרטי ים']; E950 (acesulfame-K) gained ['אססולפאם', 'א ססולפאם']. The extra two-token variants ('אספרטי ים', 'א ססולפאם') are the same words with a stray OCR/scrape space, found via corpus-wide scan on the same barcodes -- included so the same root-cause class doesn't require a second pass.
